messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing steady GPU memory growth on MI250 when running paged-KV with long-context workloads (20k tokens) and our dense batching heuristic. Not a crash, just slow climb until OOM after ~2h :confused:
chris: Can you paste the simplest repro and the eviction logs? MI vs A100 diff would help.
anika: Might be kernel selection differences on ROCm path vs cuBLAS kernels. Could be different pagewalk hot paths.
maria: repro script is tiny, runs paged attention over a 20k prompt with batch_size=8 and our continuous-batching enabled. Evict logs attached inline: 
```
[2026-02-14T14:12:02Z] kvcache: page_alloc id=0x7f3f free=128 used=872 frag=42%
[2026-02-14T14:12:32Z] kvcache: evict candidate pages=64 pinned=2 scanned=512
[2026-02-14T14:12:32Z] page_table: remap miss for slot 0x1a3a, creating shadow entry
[2026-02-14T14:12:32Z] kvcache: eviction skipped (reuse_window hit)
[2026-02-14T14:12:45Z] kvcache: page_alloc id=0x7f3f free=96 used=904 frag=46%
[2026-02-14T14:13:12Z] kvcache: growth detected: resident=24.6GB -> 25.9GB over 20m
```
maria: note the "eviction skipped (reuse_window hit)" keeps coming up even when scanned hotspots should be eligible. Evict policy seems to prefer keeping cold pages pinned on MI250.
chris: Interesting. Does the same run on A100 show the same reuse_window behavior?
maria: On A100 the reuse_window logic actually evicts expected pages when scanned; resident stays near 18GB. On MI250 it drifts up.
anika: Can you dump the kernel selection log? The runtime logs which kernel variant we pick for attention/paged-attn. If ROCm picks a different tiled-kernel that touches pages differently it could break our walk heuristic.
maria: pasted kernel log below: 
```
[rt-runtime] model=redwood-rlhf-v1 kernel=attn_paged_tile_v2 variant=rocm_tile_32x8 prefetch=on kv_layout=sharded
[rt-runtime] kernel_selector: picked rocm_tile_32x8 (lat=1.23ms) over rocm_tile_16x16 (lat=1.46ms) due to batch=8 longctx bias
[rt-runtime] pagewalker: access_pattern=long-prefix stride=1.0 scan_hint=aggressive
```
ryan: That selection makes sense perf-wise but rocm_tile_32x8 has a different access order (tile-major) vs cu kernel (row-major) which can change prefetch locality for our page table. If the page table metadata is sensitive to access order, fragmentation can increase.
chris: Any PMEM/PCIe stalls? Logs show a few nvlink-like retransmits on NVIDIA, but on MI250 we saw PCIe TLP backpressure once. Could cause delayed free/completion and pin lingering.
maria: I captured a short perf trace showing outstanding DMA refs never cleared for a shard during longctx. Snippet: 
```
shard0 outstanding_refs=0x12 -> 0x12 -> 0x12 (no decrement after eviction)
caller stack: runtime::kvpage_unpin -> runtime::evict_scan -> runtime::async_free_cb
async_free_cb never invoked (queued but never completed on rocm-stream-2)
```
anika: async_free_cb not firing smells like completion event dropped on that queue; kernel variant may use a different stream-sync pattern. Can you repro with STREAM_SYNC=1 env var and see if behavior changes?
maria: Tried STREAM_SYNC=1 — growth stops for the run (resident stays steady) but latency increases ~8%. So it's a tradeoff.
chris: Good repro. If STREAM_SYNC mitigates, then adding a fencing fix or ensuring async_free_cb scheduling is robust on ROCm path is the right fix. Could also add a defensive timeout where outstanding_refs > threshold triggers forced completion.
ryan: For immediate mitigation in prod: 1) lower reuse_window to 0.2 on MI250 fleets; 2) conservative kernel selector fallback to rocm_tile_16x16 for longctx workloads until fix. Both are low-risk flags.
maria: I ran the lower reuse_window experiment — memory growth rate dropped by ~85% over 3h. Perf penalty minimal.
chris: Can you open a small PR adding a diagnostic toggled by env var (KV_PAGE_DIAG=1) that dumps outstanding_refs per-shard periodically? It'll help confirm fix rollout.
anmaria: will do — creating PR with tests. Also filing bug with ROCm repro and trace to vendor.
dev-bot: CI job #7842 for branch kvcache/rocm-async-free started — logs: https://ci.internal/7842 :gear:
chris: Thanks. Let's track in #eng-runtime and post perf numbers after the kernel-fallback rollout. :thumbsup:
ryan: adding a canary plan: deploy reuse_window=0.2 and kernel_fallback to 10% of MI250 pool for 24h. If stable, ramp to 100%.
maria: will run the canary tomorrow morning and report results here.
